mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates accommodative monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days regardless of economic regime.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 4.0%, or Rank IC over 3-year rolling window remains below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeding 4.5% signals deteriorating labor market conditions and reduced consumer spending power, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE exceeds 4.5%, or Rank IC over 3-year rolling window remains below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates robust consumer demand, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days through accelerated corporate revenue growth.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS show positive month-over-month growth, or Rank IC for interaction term remains below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: In high-inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 3.5%), a rising federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals aggressive monetary tightening that compresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 3.5% AND FEDFUNDS increases by > 0.1pp in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods meeting trigger condition, or Rank IC for interaction term remains below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: A rising industrial production index (INDPRO) reflects strengthening manufacturing output and economic momentum, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days through improved corporate earnings visibility.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO growth exceeds 0.5% monthly, or Rank IC over 3-year rolling window remains below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: A quarterly GDP growth rate (GDPC1) below 1.0% annualized signals economic contraction, reducing corporate earnings expectations and causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when GDPC1 growth is below 1.0%, or Rank IC over 3-year rolling window remains below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: In tight labor markets (UNRATE < 4.0%), strong payroll growth (PAYEMS growth > 100) signals wage inflation pressures and potential Fed tightening, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: tight labor market with strong job growth
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods meeting trigger condition, or Rank IC for interaction term remains below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: Persistent inflation (CPIAUCSL rising) combined with stable or rising federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates unrelenting inflationary pressures that trigger equity market sell-offs, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when CPIAUCSL is rising and FEDFUNDS is stable or rising, or Rank IC for interaction term remains below 0.02.
